input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: style() tests fg and bg for truthiness instead of `is not None`, so the 256-color index 0 is skipped
- failure path: click.style('x', fg=0) or bg=0, meaning black, applies no color at all and the text renders in the terminal default; the caller sees no error

Reviewer finding
- description: The check `if fg:` replaces `if fg is not None:`, so a falsy but valid color is silently skipped. Integer color 0 (black in the 256-color palette) is dropped, as is an empty-string color.
- rationale: Trigger: `style('x', fg=0)` or `bg=0`. The falsy value fails the truthiness test, so no escape code is emitted. The user gets uncolored text instead of black with no error. The same defect applies to `bg` at line 684.
critique: The finding pins the defect on the truthiness check (`if fg:` instead of `is not None`) for both fg and bg. It also gives the same trigger as the label: color index 0 is skipped, so no escape code is emitted and the text comes out uncolored without any error. The mechanism matches the labeled defect.
